                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure can lead to damage to cranial nerves III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), VI (abducens), and V1 (trigeminal). This can result in absent left corneal reflex due to involvement of V1, which is responsible for sensory innervation to the cornea. Additionally, involvement of CN III can lead to left eye muscle paralysis, affecting eye movement. However, CN VI, which controls lateral gaze, may remain unaffected, allowing for preserved left lateral gaze. The optic nerve (CN II) may also be affected, potentially leading to complete loss of vision in the left eye, but this is less certain without direct evidence of optic nerve involvement. Therefore, the most likely physical examination finding is absent left corneal reflex due to V1 involvement.
